question.problem: A triangle $△ABC$ has $m∠A={37}^{∘},$ $m∠B={90}^{∘},$ and $AC=25.$ Find $AB$ rounded to the nearest integer.

current_example.problem:
Given the triangle below, find the length of $\overline{MN}$ rounded to one decimal place. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203245/assets/db0c3be4d3f18a55bfbd763e4017bdabd6c27ba7b498e21909baa4aea3d44337.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta$ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

- $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

- $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the hypotenuse $\overline{NO}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overline{MN}$ adjacent to the given angle $\angle{N}.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is *cosine*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(m∠N) & =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({25}^{∘}) & =\frac{MN}{14} \\ MN & =14\operatorname{cos}⁡({25}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}MN & =14\operatorname{cos}⁡({25}^{∘}) \\  & =14(0.906\,30…) \\  & =12.688\,30… \\  & ≈12.7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
